<Serbian>: 11. Maj, 1942. Mala plima je jedini znak nadolazećeg cunamija. Ovo zatišje u borbi je zabrinjavajuće. Amerkianci imaju nove letelice koje su veoma brze a mi nemamo ništa što bi im pariralo! Fokusiraćemo svo naše iskustvo na izbegavanje njihovih napada, nemoćni da uzvratimo neprijatelju. Svi naši uzleti su pod striktnom kontrolom - samo se najiskusnijim pilotima dozvoljava da se vinu u nebo. Ali naći ćemo im slabost. Ja ću je naći.
<Hungarian>: 1942. május 11. Az apály a váratlanul érkező szökőár egyetlen jele. A harcok szünetelése pedig csak a vihar előtti csend. Az amerikaiak új repülőgépeket kaptak, amik olyan gyorsak, hogy nem tudjuk utolérni őket! Minden tudásunkkal arra koncentrálunk, hogy kitérjünk a támadásaik elől, és így nem tudunk visszatámadni. A bevetéseinket szigorúan ellenőrzik, és csak a legtapasztaltabb pilótákat engedik fel a levegőbe. De meg fogjuk találni a gyengéjüket. Meg fogom találni.
<Korean>: May 11, 1942. A low tide is the only sign of the sudden arrival of a tsunami. This lull in the fighting bodes trouble. Người Mỹ có máy bay mới rất nhanh và chúng ta không có gì sánh kịp! Chúng ta tập trung toàn bộ kinh nghiệm vào việc né tránh các cuộc tấn công của họ, không thể phản công lại kẻ thù. <English>: January 3, 1943. It was easier to fight the Russians, at least in some ways. There is something similar to us in them — they go into battle with honor and fight to the very end. Even though they were far more dangerous opponents, they were still more in line with my understanding of real combat. Their strict adherence to military doctrine forbids them to decorate their planes, so you never knew whether you were facing a real ace or a rookie youngster. The Americans are different. If they fail, they rely on the speed of their new fighters to immediately escape and this happens time and time again until one of us runs out of fuel. All battles come down to evasive maneuvers and it’s rare to catch the most self-assured enemies in a dive. I’m sick of this.
<French>: 3 Janvier 1943. C'était plus simple de se battre contre les russes, d'une certaine manière. Il y a quelque chose de similaire à nous chez eux – ils se battent avec honneur et jusqu'au bout. Même s'ils étaient des adversaires plus dangereux, ils seraient plus en accord avec ma conception d'un vrai combat. Leur stricte adhésion à leur doctrine leur interdit de décorer leurs avions, donc tu ne sais jamais si tu affronte un vrai as ou un bleu. Les américains sont différents. S'ils font une erreur, ils comptent sur la vitesse de leurs nouveaux chasseurs pour s'échapper immédiatement et cela jusqu'à ce qu'ils tombent à court de carburant. Toutes les batailles se résument à des manœuvres évasives et il est rare d'attraper les ennemis les plus confiants dans un piqué. J'en ai marre.
<Italian>: 3 gennaio 1943. Era più facile combattere i russi, almeno sotto certi aspetti. C'è qualcosa di simile a noi in loro — entrano in battaglia con onore e combattono fino alla fine. Anche se erano avversari molto più pericolosi, erano più in linea con la mia comprensione del vero e proprio combattimento. La loro rigorosa dottrina militare gli proibisce di decorare i loro aerei, così non si sapeva mai se stavamo affrontando un vero asso o un novellino. Gli americani sono diversi. Se falliscono, si basano sulla velocità di loro nuovi caccia per fuggire immediatamente e questo accade di volta in volta fino a quando uno di noi finisce il carburante. Tutte le battaglie si riducono a manovre evasive ed è raro abbattere i nemici più sicuri di sé in un affondo. Sono stufo di tutto questo.
<German>: 3. Januar 1943. Es war einfacher, die Russen zu bekämpfen, zumindest in gewisser Weise. Es ist etwas Ähnliches wie bei uns in ihnen - sie gehen mit Ehre in den Kampf und kämpfen bis zum Ende. Obwohl sie weitaus gefährlichere Gegner waren, entsprachen sie dennoch mehr meinem Verständnis von echtem Kampf. Ihre strikte Befolgung der Militärdoktrin verbietet es ihnen, ihre Flugzeuge zu dekorieren, so dass man nie wusste, ob man es mit einem echten Ass oder einem Neuling zu tun hatte. Die Amerikaner sind anders. Wenn sie scheitern, verlassen sie sich auf die Geschwindigkeit ihrer neuen Kampfflugzeuge, um sofort zu entkommen, und das passiert immer wieder, bis einem von uns der Treibstoff ausgeht. Alle Kämpfe laufen auf Ausweichmanöver hinaus und nur selten erwischt man die selbstbewusstesten Feinde bei einem Sturzflug. Ich habe genug davon.
<Spanish>: 3 de Enero de 1943. Era más fácil luchar contra los Rusos, al menos en algunos aspectos. Hay algo parecido a nosotros en ellos - van a la batalla con honor y luchan hasta el final. Aunque eran adversarios mucho más peligrosos, se ajustaban más a mi forma de entender el combate real. Su estricta adhesión a la doctrina militar les prohíbe decorar sus aviones, así que nunca sabías si te enfrentabas a un verdadero as o a un joven novato. Los americanos son diferentes. Si fallan, confían en la velocidad de sus nuevos cazas para escapar inmediatamente y esto sucede una y otra vez hasta que uno de los dos se queda sin combustible. Todas las batallas se reducen a maniobras evasivas y es raro atrapar a los enemigos más seguros de sí mismos en una maniobra de inmersión. Estoy harto de esto.
<Russian>: 3 января 1943 года. С русскими было как-то проще сражаться. Они чем-то похожи на нас – принимали бой честно и бились до последнего. Будучи гораздо более опасными противниками, они все же лучше вписывались в мое понимание настоящего боя, а их следование уставу, запрещавшему разукрашивать свои самолеты, скрывало от тебя: ас это или начинающий мальчуган, и было по настоящему страшно. Американцы действуют не так. Если у них не получилось, они, полагаясь на скорость своих новых истребителей, тут же уходят, и так десятки раз, пока у одного из нас не кончится топливо. Все сражения сводятся к маневрам-уклонения, лишь в редких случаях удается поймать самых самоуверенных в пике. Надоело.
<Polish>: 3 stycznia 1943 roku. Było łatwiej walczyć z Rosjanami, przynajmniej pod pewnymi względami. Mają w sobie coś podobnego do nas - wchodzą do walki z honorem i walczą do samego końca. Nawet mimo że byli o wiele bardziej niebezpiecznymi przeciwnikami, wciąż bardziej odpowiadali mojemu pojęciu o prawdziwej walce. Ich ścisłe przestrzeganie doktryny wojskowej zabrania im dekorowania swoich samolotów, więc nigdy nie wiedziałeś, czy masz do czynienia z prawdziwym asem czy z nowicjuszem. Amerykanie są inni. Jeśli zawiodą, polegają na szybkości swoich nowych myśliwców, by natychmiast uciec i to dzieje się raz za razem, aż któremuś z nas zabraknie paliwa. Wszystkie bitwy sprowadzają się do uników i rzadko zdarza się złapać najbardziej pewnych siebie wrogów w locie nurkowym. Mam tego dość.
<Czech>: 3. ledna 1943. Bylo to snazší bojovat proti Rusům, alespoň v některých ohledech. V něčem se nám podobají – jdou do boje s ctít a bojují až do samého konce. I když byli mnohem nebezpečnějšími protivníky, pořád odpovídali mému chápání skutečného boje. Striktně omezovali označení svých letadel, takže jste nikdy nevěděli, zda čelíte skutečnému esu nebo mladému nováčkovi. Američané jsou jiní. Pokud v útoku neuspějou, spoléhají schopnost svých nových stíhaček rychle uletět a opakují to pořád dokola, dokud jednomu z nás nedojde palivo. Všechny bitvy se redukovaly na úhybné manévry a je vzácné zachytit sebevědomého nepřítele při klesání. Je mi z toho na nic.
<Turkish>: 3 Ocak 1943. Ruslarla savaşmak daha kolaydı, en azından bazı açılardan. Onlarda bize benzer bir şeyler var - savaşa onurla giriyorlar ve sonuna kadar savaşıyorlar. Çok daha tehlikeli rakipler olmalarına rağmen, benim gerçek savaş anlayışıma daha uygunlardı. Askeri doktrine sıkı sıkıya bağlı olmaları uçaklarını süslemelerini yasaklıyordu, bu yüzden karşınızda gerçek bir as mı yoksa çaylak bir genç mi olduğunu asla bilemiyordunuz. Amerikalılar farklıdır. Eğer başarısız olurlarsa, hemen kaçmak için yeni avcı uçaklarının hızına güveniyorlar ve bu, birimizin yakıtı bitene kadar defalarca tekrarlanıyor. Tüm savaşlar kaçış manevralarına dayanıyor ve kendine en çok güvenen düşmanları bir dalışta yakalamak nadiren mümkün oluyor. Bıktım artık bundan.

<Serbian>: 3. Januar, 1943. Bilo je lakše boriti se sa Rusima, barem na neki način. Ima nešto slično u nama - oni idu u bitku časno i bore se do samog kraja. <English>: September 23, 1944. I couldn’t sleep. I’m not the only one — the crew wanders around the ship listlessly, like nori leaves swaying in the current. Our aircraft carrier is being sent from port to port over the last few months and we are sitting around without any clear understanding of the situation. Of course, they never tell us anything, but when the crew is so close that you are having strong drinks in the middle of the night with the first mate instead of getting some healthy sleep the situation becomes clearer. I have just spent half an hour staring into space before I could snap out of it. Let’s stop lying to ourselves — there’s no chance. We have lost this war, but we must keep doing our duties as the Emperor’s faithful warriors, even if its done purely through force of habit, at least until the Emperor orders us to put down our weapons and come home. It’s funny that it is only now that I have begun to realize how much I miss my family. They have ordered us to scramble – bombers are coming. I feel like something bad is about to happen...

Bien sûr, ils ne nous disent jamais rien, mais quand l'équipage est si proche que vous buvez des boissons fortes au milieu de la nuit avec le second au lieu de vous reposer, la situation devient plus claire. J'ai contemplé le ciel une demi-heure avant de retrouver mon calme. Arrêtons de nous mentir — nous n'avons aucune chance. Nous avons perdu cette guerre, mais nous devons continuer à servir l'Empereur comme de fidèles guerriers, même si ce n'est que par habitude, au moins jusqu'à ce que l'Empereur nous ordonne de déposer les armes et de rentrer à la maison. C'est drôle que ce ne soit que maintenant que je me rendes compte que ma famille me manque beaucoup. On nous a ordonné de décoller – des bombardiers arrivent. J'ai l'impression que quelque chose de mauvais se prépare...

Abbiamo perso questa guerra, ma dobbiamo continuare a fare i nostri doveri come fedeli guerrieri dell'imperatore, anche se il oramai è solo puramente la forza dell'abitudine, almeno fino a quando gli ordini dell'imperatore ci impongono di deporre le nostre armi e tornare a casa. La cosa divertente è che solo ora che ho cominciato a rendermi conto di quanto mi manca la mia famiglia. Ci hanno ordinato di intercettare i bombardieri che stanno arrivando. Mi sento che qualcosa di brutto sta per accadere...
<German>: 23. September 1944. Ich konnte nicht schlafen. Ich bin nicht der Einzige - die Besatzung wandert lustlos um das Schiff herum, so wie Nori sich in der Strömung wiegt. Unser Flugzeugträger wird in den letzten Monaten von Hafen zu Hafen geschickt, und wir sitzen herum, ohne ein klares Verständnis für die Situation zu haben. Natürlich sagen sie uns nie etwas, aber wenn die Besatzung so nahe ist, dass man mitten in der Nacht mit dem ersten Maat starke Drinks zu sich nimmt, anstatt gesund zu schlafen, wird die Situation klarer. Ich habe gerade eine halbe Stunde lang in den Weltraum gestarrt, bevor ich wieder aufwachen konnte. Hören wir auf, uns selbst zu belügen - es gibt keine Chance. Wir haben diesen Krieg verloren, aber wir müssen weiterhin unsere Pflichten als treue Krieger des Kaisers erfüllen, auch wenn dies nur aus Gewohnheit geschieht, zumindest so lange, bis der Kaiser uns befiehlt, die Waffen niederzulegen und nach Hause zu kommen. Es ist komisch, dass mir erst jetzt bewusst wird, wie sehr ich meine Familie vermisse. Sie haben uns befohlen, aufzubrechen - die Bomber kommen. Ich habe das Gefühl, dass etwas Schlimmes passieren wird...

Полчаса смотрел в одну точку перед тем, как продолжить. Не будем обманывать себя – шансов нет. Мы проиграли эту войну и просто по привычке выполняем свой долг, как преданные войны императора, до указа самого императора сложить оружие и вернуться домой. Забавно, только сейчас начинаю осознавать, как скучаю по семье. Дали команду на вылет – бомбардировщики. У меня нехорошее предчувствие...
<Polish>: 23 września 1944 roku. Nie mogłem spać. Nie jestem jedyny - załoga włóczy się po statku bez zapału, jak nori unoszone prądem. Nasz lotniskowiec był wysyłany z portu do portu przez ostatnie kilka miesięcy, a my siedzimy bez jasnego zrozumienia sytuacji. Oczywiście, nigdy nam nic nie mówią, ale gdy załoga jest tak blisko, że w nocy pijesz mocne napoje z pierwszym oficerem zamiast zdrowo się wyspać, sytuacja staje się jaśniejsza. Przed chwilą spędziłem pół godziny patrząc w przestrzeń, zanim się otrząsnąłem. Przestańmy się oszukiwać - nie ma szans. Przegraliśmy tę wojnę, ale musimy nadal wykonywać nasze obowiązki jako wierni wojownicy Cesarza, nawet jeśli robi się to tylko przez siłę przyzwyczajenia, przynajmniej do czasu, gdy Cesarz rozkaże nam odłożyć broń i wrócić do domu. Právě jsem strávil půl hodiny zíráním do prázdna, než jsem se z toho dostal. Přestaňme si něco nalhávat – není žádná šance. <English>: My Dearest Love, It's hard to put the first few days into words. You hear stories but you can never be prepared for what you experience on those first combat sorties. Constant waves of fighters being thrown across the Channel at us, it was the sort of wake-up call none of my squadron saw coming. As soon as that scramble bell rings, you know they are coming. You know you have just minutes before they are on you. Every second a precious moment you can't afford to waist. You have to be quicker than quick and faster than fast. It becomes a routine that you soon forget all about. You scramble, you fight, you touch down and then it's just a matter of time until you start over. This war feels like it has no end.

Tu sais que tu n'as que quelques minutes avant qu'ils ne soient sur toi. Chaque seconde est un moment précieux que tu ne peux pas te permettre de perdre. Tu dois être le plus rapide possible et plus encore. Cela devient une telle routine que tu oublies tout. Tu décolles, tu voles, tu te bats et puis c'est une question de temps avant que cela ne recommence. Cette guerre semble ne pas avoir de fin.

I caccia arrivano incessanti attraverso il canale fino a noi, era il tipo di sveglia che nessuno del mio squadrone ha mai sentito. Appena la campana suona, sai che sono arrivati. Sai che hai pochi minuti prima che siano su di noi. Ogni secondo ė un prezioso momento in cui ci si può rimettere la vita.  Devi essere più veloce, più veloce e più veloce ancora. Si trasforma in una routine in cui ci si dimentica presto di tutto il resto. Si corre, si lotta, si torna giú e quindi è solo una questione di tempo fino a quando non ce se ne accorge più. Sembra che questa guerra non finisca mai.

<English>: Its me again, sweetheart. I just had my third sortie of the day, the standard air patrol around the base. We were climbing at the regular 20 degrees, to have the best view of our base, while we were at it. Ginger Tom spotted a low flying group of unknowns off to the southeast, my heart was in my throat, you know that feeling when something's about to happen and the focus is on you. Our leader ordered us to break and engage; we peeled off one at a time and took a gentle corkscrew down to engage the targets. Stukas! Without an escort! My ears were ringing. As I pulled out of the dive, I raked an enemy fuselage from wing to wing, there was a lot of bits and pieces of wing peeling off from the victim. His gunner was spraying shots to the rear, in panic as there was nothing there, the their aircraft tilted hard left and started to fall, billowing unspent fuel into the air. I circled round in front to confirm the kill, watching as the Ju-87 ploughed its way through a barley field and into a drystone wall. It looked like they crew both climbed out the downed aircraft, ah well, at least they would get some proper rest tonight.

<English>: Not sure how much more I can go without sleep, my feet dance in bed, i can’t settle down, I’m watching dear friends disappear from the roster day after day and half expecting not to come back each time I get up. We can’t seem to find replacements quick enough and the regular bomber intercept missions we are running are taking a huge toll on our strength. At least we are intercepting them before they reach the land. If I go down, I’ll get a softer landing. I wish knew how to swim, though. I wonder what the bomber crews are thinking, are they different to us? I don’t expect they are. On the positive side, it looks like our comrades in arms from other countries like Poland are joining the fight and forming their own fighter squadrons, great, those guys are fantastic pilots and damn brave soldiers.

Nous ne parvenons pas à trouver des remplaçants assez rapidement et les missions régulières d'interception de bombardiers qui nous font courir, pèsent lourdement sur nos forces. Au moins, nous les interceptons avant qu'ils atteignent le pays. Si je suis touché, je pourrai atterrir facilement. Je voudrais bien savoir nager, quoique ... Je me demande si les équipages des bombardiers pensent nous? Je ne m'attends pas à ce que ce soit le cas. Pour les cotés positifs, il semble que nos camarades des autres pays comme la Pologne aient rejoint la bataille et formé leurs propres escadrilles de chasseurs, bien; Ces gars sont de fantastiques pilotes et de sacrés bons soldats.
<Italian>: Non sono sicuro di quanto posso stare senza dormire, sto sveglio sul letto, non riesco a rilassarmi, ogni giorno vedo cari amici che scompaiono e l'altra metà in attesa di tornare. Non riusciamo a trovare sostituti abbastanza velocemente e le missioni di intercettazione dei Bombardieri ci stanno prosciugando le forze. Almeno riusciamo ad intercettarli prima che raggiungano la nostra terra. Se prescipito, effettuo un atterraggio morbido. Vorrei saper nuotare, però. Mi chiedo che cosa stanno pensando le squadre dei bombardieri, sono diversi da noi? Non mi aspetto che lo siano. Il lato positivo, sembra che i nostri compagni d'armi da altri paesi come la Polonia stiano unendosi alla lotta, formando i propri squadroni di caccia, grandi, quei ragazzi sono fantastici piloti e soldati dannatamente coraggiosi.
<German>: Ich weiß nicht, wie viel mehr ich noch ohne Schlaf auskommen kann, meine Füße tanzen im Bett, ich kann mich nicht beruhigen, sehe, wie enge Freunde Tag für Tag von der Einsatzliste verschwinden und jedes Mal, wenn ich aufstehe, rechne ich fast damit, dass sie nicht zurückkommen. Es sieht nicht danach aus, als ob wir Ersatzkräfte schnell genug finden können und unsere regulären Bomberabfangmissionen zehren enorm an unseren Kräften. Immerhin fangen wir sie ab, bevor sie Land erreichen. Falls ich abstürze, habe ich eine weichere Landung, ich wüsste aber gerne, wie man schwimmt. Ich frage mich, was die Bomberbesatzungen denken, sind sie anders als wir? Ich denke nicht. Positiv ist, es sieht so aus, dass sich unsere Waffenbrüder aus anderen Ländern, wie Polen, dem Kampf anschließen und eigene Jägerstaffel aufstellen, sehr gut, diese Typen sind fantastische Piloten und verdammt mutige Soldaten.
<Spanish>: No estoy seguro de cuánto más podré aguantar sin dormir, mis pies bailan en la cama, no puedo asentarme, estoy viendo a queridos amigos desaparecer de la lista día tras día y medio esperando no volver cada vez que me levanto. Świetnie, ci goście są fantastycznymi pilotami i cholernie odważnymi żołnierzami.

Naštěstí se zdá, že naši kamarádi z armád dalších zemí jako Polsko a Československo se chtějí zapojit do boje a vytváří vlastní stíhací perutě. Skvělé, tihle kluci jsou fantastičtí piloti a zatraceně stateční vojáci.

<English>: I can’t believe it, Tuck is gone, I feel really empty now as we had so much in common. He was engaged, his wedding was planned next month, I hope I never leave you like this. <English>: Losing someone in this war is something most people have experienced. However getting a chance at vengeance for a dear friend is something few can hope for. The same Fighter Wing of Bf 109 G10’s that took down Tuck met our bombers today. Protecting the bombers was our primary objective, but it's hard to pass up an opportunity like that. You tend to forget orders, training and procedure in moments like that. You don't think, you just act… I’ve shot him down in a dogfight, my friend Burnaby Tuck’s has been avenged.I hope to be with you again soon.Forever yours,Owen

On a tendance à oublier les ordres, l'entraînement et les procédures dans ce genre de moments. Tu ne penses pas, tu agis… Je l'ai abattu, mon ami Burnaby Tuck est vengé. J'espère être à nouveau bientôt avec toi. Pour toujours, Owen

Proteggere i bombardieri era il nostro obiettivo principale, ma è difficile farsi scappare un'occasione come quella. Tendi a dimenticare gli ordini, l'allenamento e le procedure in quei momenti. Non pensi, agisci e basta... l'ho abbattuto in uno scontro ravvicinato, il mio amico Burnaby Tuck è stato vendicato. Spero di stare con te di nuovo presto. Per sempre tuo, Owen
<German>: Jemanden in diesen Krieg zu verlieren ist etwas, das die meisten Leute erfahren haben. Unsere Bomber zu schützen war unsere Hauptaufgabe, aber was war hart eine solche Gelegenheit gehen zu lassen. Du bist in solchen Momenten kurz davor, Befehle, Training, und Prozeduren zu vergessen. Du denkst nicht, sondern du agierst einfach... Ich habe ihn in einem Luftkampf abgeschossen, mein Freund Burnaby Tuck wurde gerächt. Ich hoffe, bald wieder bei dir zu sein. Für immer deins, Owen.

<English>: Dear John,Well, it’s finally over. Our training’s finished, done, completed, out of the way. I told you my friend, flight school wouldn’t last forever, and sure, it was long, it was difficult, and it was at times painful, but with the sense of accomplishment I am feeling now, I have no doubt that you too agree that this was all worth it. We’re going to be getting our own sets of wings John! Can you believe it? I have to say, I am never going to forget our graduation from Kelly Field, and oh boy, our celebration at the after party is something I don’t think anyone will remember that night in any kind of detail! Anyway, it feels weird writing a letter to you like this, and I kind of miss being able to chat like we used to. It all feels so sudden; everything’s happening so quickly. It won’t be long before we’re deployed. Wouldn’t it be funny if we were placed in the same squadron? What better way to settle our rivalry! Anyway, I hope everything’s been well for you since we last spoke. I hope we get the chance to catch up before long. Take care my friend.

<English>: Dear John,She is an absolute beauty… The Grumman F4F Wildcat is the most beautiful aircraft I have ever seen. <English>: Dear John,The first thing I want you to know is that I’m alive. No doubt you’ve been hearing reports of the damage here at Pearl Harbor. <English>: Dear John,I really get it now. I get my place here. I am an airman of the United States, protecting our fleet from harm, and I will not let harm come to my fellow comrades. We’ve been engaging waves of Japanese fighters as of late. With my wings repaired and ready once more, I feel our training has really come through. Yesterday, our carrier was attacked, We scrambled to engage the enemy. Amidst all the flying and fighting, I went head to head with a Zero fighter. You know how some say that time can slow down? We fire at one another, and both turned at the last second, but there, I look him straight in the eye. I glared back at me, his face a statue of chiselled determination. Time slowed down here, John, I swear it… I didn’t see him again. I wonder if he made it home… I wonder if he was lucky… Take care my friend.

<English>: To my good friend Glen,Into Western Europe we go. Into the thick of it, taking on danger, staring it straight in the eye. I knew this would happen when I volunteered for this. They’ve replaced my wings with a P-51 Mustang. The grunt of its engine is like none other I have heard. My mission was to escort some B-17s. It seems they really live up to their name as the ‘flying fortress’. I swear, I have seen them land despite being torn to shreds, missing sections of their tail, and even parts of their wings. I wonder if the same damage to my aircraft would have a different effect… I wonder… Am I surviving on borrowed time? Why have I been so lucky…?

<English>: To my good friend Glen,We often find ourselves flying with the Canadians and the Brits. Now, let me tell you, these guys can fly. Edward, one of the RAF guys who flies a Spit, saved my life yesterday. A 109 tailed me, chipping away at the delicate parts of my fuselage. I radioed out: "Taking fire". Well, the sound of two engines changes to three, and I’m sure the bullets that were flying past me doubled. Well, it wasn’t long before the fire stopped for good. He flew up alongside me, grinned widely, and gave me both thumbs up. It certainly was, as I’ve heard them say, a "jolly good show".

J'ai envoyé par radio: "Je me fais tirer dessus". Eh bien, le son de deux moteurs est passé à trois et je suis sûr que les balles qui me frôlaient se sont dédoublées. <English>: To my good friend Glen,I’m really getting the feel for this P-51 now. It's amazing the things this bird can do when you treat her right. The speed and performance, it feels worlds apart from those rust buckets we were flying years ago back in Texas. I did have a soft spot for those P-39s, but I think the Mustangs got my heart now. We’re still protecting the heavies to their targets deep into Germany, but those guys really are getting desperate now. We hear stories of new aircraft every day, all these strange rumors about German jets and rocket, never know what to expect on a mission now. Every day it seems we get more and more frontline squadrons arriving and we push further and further across Europe. Still, hopefully this damned war will be over soon and we can all go home.

J'avais un faible pour ces P-39, mais je pense que les Mustang ont conquis mon cœur maintenant. Nous protégeons toujours les bombardiers lourds au dessus de l'Allemagne, mais ces gars-là sont vraiment désespérés maintenant. Nous entendons des histoires de nouveaux avions tous les jours, toutes ces rumeurs étranges sur les jets et les fusées allemands, on ne sait jamais à quoi s'attendre en mission maintenant. Chaque jour, il semble que de plus en plus d'escadrons de première ligne arrivent et que nous poussons de plus en plus loin à travers l'Europe. Pourtant, j'espère que cette maudite guerre sera bientôt terminée et que nous pourrons tous rentrer chez nous.

La velocità e le prestazioni, ci si sente su un mondo a parte in confronto a quelle carrette con cui volavamo anni fa in Texas. Ho un debole per i P-39, ma penso che i Mustang abbiano rapito il mio cuore in questo momento. Stiamo ancora proteggendo i pesanti sui loro bersagli all'interno della Germania, quei ragazzi sono davvero sempre più disperati. Abbiamo sentito storie di nuovi aerei ogni giorno, girano strane voci su aerei a getto e a razzo tedeschi, non puoi mai sapere cosa ti aspetta in una missione in questo momento. Ogni giorno sembra che si aggiungano sempre più squadriglie di bombardieri e che noi spingiamo ulteriormente in tutta Europa. Speriamo che questa maledetta guerra finisca presto e che possiamo tutti andare a casa.

Ich habe ein Fable für diese P-39, aber ich denke, die Mustangs haben jetzt mein Herz. Wir schützen immer noch die schweren Bomber zu ihren Zielen tief in Deutschland, aber diese Jungs werden immer mehr verzeifelter. Wir hören jeden Tag Geschichten von neuen Flugzeugen, all diese verrückten Gerüchte von deutschen Düsen- und Raketenflugzeugen, du weißt nie, was dich jetzt auf einer Mission erwartet. Jeden Tag sieht es so aus, als ob wir mehr und mehr Frontstaffeln ankommen und wir weiter und weiter über Europa vorrücken. Trotzdem, hoffentlich wird dieser verdammte Krieg bald vorbei sein und wir können alle nach Hause gehen.

<English>: We were sitting at a forward base yesterday, when we noticed a German scout aircraft buzzing around. He circled above us for half an hour, and then disappeared. Next thing we know, we are being attacked by a group of Stukas, I watched the AA defence getting into position and our tank crews were assisting where they could by bringing extra ammo and calling out targets. You remember Joe Degriss, a guy that went to school with me in Bronx? He was here, commanding one of the M16 AA Carriages, him and his crew wiped out a Stuka that seemed to be determined to cause trouble. But the guys did it! I have never thought that a half track could be so effective.

<English>: Hello folks! Our platoon is moving forward again, the roads are full of civilians and it is tough going through the masses of refugees going the opposite way. It is hard watching the road ahead, scouring all them hedges and the trees for potential trouble, which isn't made any easier by the threat of German bombers. Some pockets of resistance remain behind us, but it is important to keep driving forward and leave the proper clearing out of the enemy strugglers to our infantry. I still can't understand what is driving ordinary soldiers like us and Germans to be hurling lethal lumps of metal at each other, I guess they must think they are fighting for the same reasons we are. We are still finding enemy tank destroyers and other armor hidden away in superb ambush positions, there is no doubt that German combat troops are fantastically efficient and damn fine soldiers.Jonathan

<English>: Well, ain’t I’m a lucky guy? In what has become almost boring daily routine, I got careless, and my crew nearly died as a result. I was so busy trying to catch some shut eye in an upright position in the commander’s cupola, I completely missed the German Pak 42 cannon barrel sticking out of one of the windows in a burned out church we were passing. The shot that woke me and my buddies bounced off the front of the turret, but just barely. The troops behind us, camped in one of the bocages west of us , spotted a flash from the enemy shot and opened up on the building, bringing down the wall over a hidden Jagdpanzer IV. This was all too late, as a second shot from the German tank destroyer, took out our engine and set us on fire. We managed to bail, but it was touch and go for a while. I hope that is my only close encounter I will have to be a part of. No more sleeping on duty for me and my buddies!

<English>: The battalion has provided me and my crewmates with a brand new Sherman Jumbo, its up-armored front gives us extra protection and confidence. It wasn't long before it got its first taste of some real combat action. We were attempting to flank a Tiger, that was holding back our advance from behind a a railway bank. The Tiger’s crew must have felt very confident, especially after taking out three of our M4’s. We gunned the engine, hoping to outmaneuver their turret, but that Tiger fired blind and actually hit us! But, our reinforced gun mantlet shrugged off the shot like it was nothing and we continued going fast, trying to get behind him, watching his turret slowly struggling to keep up with us. Finally, we were in position before they had a chance to fire again and that was our chance, we fired a 75mm shell into its rear, taking out the armored beast in an instant. The funny thing is, that after we were done with it, I shared a cup of cocoa with the commander of that tank. Even though none of us could to speak the other’s language, we both smiled with relief of our survival.Your son, Jonathan

Il n'a pas attendu très longtemps avant de goûter à un vrai combat. Nous tentions de flanquer un Tigre qui bloquait notre avance de derrière des chemins de fer. L'équipage du Tigre a du se sentir très confiant, surtout après avoir détruit 3 de nos M4. On a tiré sur le moteur, espérant être plus rapides que sa tourelle mais il a tiré à l'aveugle et nous a touché! Cependant, notre masque de canon renforcé a absorbé le tir comme si de rien n'était et nous avons accéléré, essayant d'arriver derrière lui, regardant sa tourelle tourner avec difficulté vers nous. Nous avions finalement atteint notre position et avons saisi notre chance, on a tiré un obus de 75 mm dans son arrière, détruisant la bête en un instant. Le plus drôle, c'est qu'après en avoir terminé, j'ai partagé une tasse de chocolat avec le commandant du Tigre. Même si nous ne parlions pas la même langue, nous pouvions nous réjouir d'avoir survécu ensemble.Votre fils, Jonathan

Ma, il nostro mantello del cannone rinforzato ha respinto il colpo come se niente fosse ed abbiamo continuato ad avanzare velocemente, cercando di arrivare dietro di lui, guardando sua torretta girare lentamente per tenerci sotto mira. Infine, eravamo in posizione prima che avessero la possibilità di sparare di nuovo ed è stata la nostra occasione, abbiamo sparato un proiettile da 75mm nella sua parte posteriore, mettendo fuori combattimento la bestia blindata in un istante. La cosa divertente è che dopo abbiamo condiviso una tazza di cioccolato con il comandante di quel carro armato. Anche se nessuno di noi poteva parlare la lingua dell'altro, entrambi abbiamo sorriso con sollievo della nostra sopravvivenza. Vostro figlio, Jonathan

Мы были уверены, что проскочим быстрее, чем он повернет башню, но "Тигр" выстрелил наудачу и попал в нас! Однако все-таки удача была не на его стороне, орудийная маска на нашем красавце без проблем отбросила снаряд, а мы погнали дальше, заходя ему в тыл и наблюдая, как медленно поворачивается его башня. Мы заняли позицию раньше, чем он смог снова выстрелить, и пустили ему в корму 75-мм снаряд, который сразу вывел этого бронированного монстра из строя. <English>: I know I said we would never sleep again, but I guess i was wrong there. For a second time, we came close to death by simply being too tired. So, me and my boys were tight asleep. The engine was still warm and the night was cold. I again was atop our Jumbo, resting on the tank’s turret, with my arms over my eyes. The rest of the crew were propped up against the tracks on the ground, wrapped in a bunch of old blankets. I woke to the sound of an explosion behind our tank, only to see a fireball lighting up the night some five hundred yards behind us. Turns out, Rob Arthur’s M18 crew were playing cards when they heard some commotion off to the left of their position, they couldn't see anything but fired up their vehicle hoping the other tanks scattered about the forest patch would hear them. They cranked the turret in the general direction of the sound of unknown engines, when they spotted an outline of a German panzer against the twilight. They caught the Germans by surprise, while other unseen contacts have retreated back into the darkness, repelled by our alerted response. I really must buy Rob Arthur’s crew some drinks next time we're in town.

<English>: Mom, Dad, I'm sure that when you get this letter, the war will be over. Our troops are advancing very fast and it looks like we will not meet any more serious resistance. Towns surrender one after another, but I still have to fight and take care of my crew every day. In Stuttgart a few of our Shermans bayed a large, steelclad German cat – it was a Tiger heavy tank. The Germans fought bravely and there shot took out one of ours, but my crew managed to jam their turret and set their engine on fire. The German tank crew survived, and then we then captured them. Here we have the British and Canadian allies fighting side-by-side, we will soon have to meet with Russians, they are very close. Hitler does not have a prayer now. Soon, the war will end and i’m coming home!I hope to see you all soon.Your son, Jonathan

<English>: It was late autumn of 1940 when our regiment was visited by the designers of our new T-34 tank. Since I was highly rated during my service and studies, the command ordered me to go to the training grounds with the engineers and test the tank under their instruction. While traversing a particularly difficult obstacle, i blew out the engine block of my tank. I was very upset, but the head of the group of engineers embraced me with a smile and said that "This data is priceless to make the chassis more reliable." I really liked this new tank and really wanted the engineers to fix it’s teething problems as soon as they could. This is how I met a future tank legend.

Puisque j'ai été exemplaire durant mon service et mes études, le commandement m'ordonna de me rendre aux terrains d'entraînement avec les ingénieurs et de tester le char sous leur direction. Lors de la traversée d'un obstacle particulièrement difficile, le bloc moteur de mon char lâcha. J'étais très en colère, mais l'ingénieur en chef m'embrassa avec sourire et dit "Ces données sont inestimables pour rendre le châssis plus fiable." J'aimais vraiment ce nouveau char et souhaitais que les ingénieurs puissent corriger ses problèmes de jeunesse dès que possible. C'est comme ça que j'ai rencontré une future légende des blindés.

Sono rimasto molto deluso, ma il capo del gruppo di ingegneri mi abbracciò con un sorriso dicendomi che "questi dati sono impagabili per rendere il telaio più affidabile". Mi è piaciuto molto questo nuovo carro e gli ingegneri volevano davvero risolvere il problema non appena poterono. Questo è come ho incontrato una futura leggenda dei carri armati.

<English>: In the early hours of dawn on June 22nd, 1941, the citizens of our country were peacefully sleeping in their homes. The bright summer sun was rising into the sky from the east, children were quietly slumbering in their cribs and people were making plans for their summery Sunday. At the same time, the flame of the most terrible war to ever engulf humanity was being lit at our western borders, with the first explosions of German bombs, the sound of the tracks of German tanks on our roads and fascist soldiers marching steadily towards our cities and villages. <English>: Our regimental commander Colonel Papanov turned out to be both a decisive leader and a competent analyst. It is to him, that we owe our lives to in the first day of the war. He managed to efficiently organize the relocation of our garrison – only a few hours before that location was completely destroyed by fascist bombardment. Our tank battalions managed to not only survive, but actually set up an ambush for the Germans – we hit the rear end of a column of enemy vehicles and infantry at a river crossing, cutting off their lines of retreat. Our tanks were breaking through from the tail of the column to the river, crushing supply trucks and towed artillery, while annihilating closely packed tanks and infantry. The ranks of the invaders were consumed by panic – they tried to turn their guns on us but they failed to mount any serious resistance. The battle was short, but the river ran red with blood of enemy soldiers. Their division was demoralized and routed, crushed by our tanks. This is the way we met the enemy upon our land, the land they wished to enslave. But this small victory could not stop the enemy hordes and we had several long and ugly years of war ahead of us.

Nos bataillons de chars ont non seulement réussi à survivre mais ont aussi tendu une embuscade aux allemands – nous avons frappé l'arrière d'une colonne de véhicules ennemis à un passage de rivière, coupant leurs lignes de retraite. Nos chars roulaient de l'arrière de la colonne à la rivière, écrasant les camions de ravitaillement et l'artillerie tractée, tout en annihilant les chars et l'infanterie. Les rangs de l'envahisseur étaient pris de panique – ils tentèrent de contre-attaquer mais ne réussirent pas à opposer quelque forme de résistance que ce soit. La bataille fut courte et la rivière était rouge du sang des soldats ennemis. Leur division était démoralisée et mise en déroute, écrasée par nos chars. C'est ainsi que nous avons rencontré l'ennemi sur nos terres, la terre qu'ils souhaitaient asservir. Néanmoins cette victoire ne pouvait pas arrêter les hordes ennemies et plusieurs longues années de cette horrible guerre nous attendaient.

I nostri battaglioni corazzati sono riusciti non solo a sopravvivere, ma anche ad attuare un'imboscata ai tedeschi – abbiamo colpito la parte posteriore di una colonna di fanteria mentre attraversava un fiume, tagliando le loro linee di ritirata dei veicoli nemici. I nostri carri armati sfondarono da dietro la colonna, distruggendo i camion cisterna e le artiglierie da traino, mentre i carri armati e la fanteria vennero annichiliti. La battaglia fu breve, ma il fiume si colorò del rosso del sangue dei soldati nemici. La loro divisione era demoralizzata, schiacciata dai nostri carri armati. In questo modo abbiamo incontrato il nemico sulla nostra terra, la terra che volevano rendere schiava. Ma questa piccola vittoria non poteva fermare le orde nemiche ed avremmo avuto ancora diversi anni di lunghi e brutti scontri davanti a noi.

<Polish>: Nasz pułkowy dowódca pułkownik Papanow okazał się zarówno zdecydowanym przywódcą, jak i kompetentnym analitykiem. To jemu zawdzięczamy nasze życia w pierwszym dniu wojny. Udało mu się sprawnie zorganizować przeniesienie naszej placówki - tylko kilka godzin przed tym, jak to miejsce zostało całkowicie zniszczone przez faszystowskie bombardowanie. Nasze bataliony czołgów nie tylko przetrwały, ale faktycznie urządziły zasadzkę na Niemców - uderzyliśmy w tył kolumny pojazdów i piechoty w miejscu przeprawy przez rzekę, odcinając im drogi odwrotu. Nasze czołgi przełamywały się od końca kolumny do rzeki, miażdżąc zaopatrzeniowe ciężarówki i holowaną artylerie, jednocześnie unicestwiając gęsto ustawione czołgi i piechotę. Szeregi najeźdźców ogarnęła panika - próbowali skierować swoje działa na nas, ale nie byli w stanie stawić żadnego poważnego oporu. Bitwa była krótka, ale rzeka spłynęła krwią wrogich żołnierzy. Ich dywizja była zdemoralizowana i rozbita, zmiażdżona przez nasze czołgi. W ten sposób spotkaliśmy wroga na naszej ziemi, ziemi, którą chcieli zniewolić. Ale to małe zwycięstwo nie mogło powstrzymać hord wroga, a przed nami miały być jeszcze długie i brudne lata wojny.
<Czech>: Our regimental commander Colonel Papanov turned out to be both a decisive leader and a competent analyst. It is to him, that we owe our lives to in the first day of the war. He managed to efficiently organize the relocation of our garrison – only a few hours before that location was completely destroyed by fascist bombardment. Our tank battalions managed to not only survive, but actually set up an ambush for the Germans – we hit the rear end of a column of enemy vehicles and infantry at a river crossing, cutting off their lines of retreat. Our tanks were breaking through from the tail of the column to the river, crushing supply trucks and towed artillery, while annihilating closely packed tanks and infantry. The ranks of the invaders were consumed by panic – they tried to turn their guns on us but they failed to mount any serious resistance. The battle was short, but the river ran red with blood of enemy soldiers. Their division was demoralized and routed, crushed by our tanks. This is the way we met the enemy upon our land, the land they wished to enslave. But this small victory could not stop the enemy hordes and we had several long and ugly years of war ahead of us.

İşgalcilerin safları paniğe kapılmıştı - silahlarını bize çevirmeye çalıştılar ama ciddi bir direniş gösteremediler. Savaş kısa sürdü ama nehir düşman askerlerinin kanıyla kıpkırmızı oldu. <English>: Our battalion assumed a defensive position near Nevel with an order to halt the enemy’s advance towards Moscow. I hit a German tank at the very beginning of the battle, but the tank’s crew managed to turn their gun at us, soon after their armor piercing shell hit the turret of our T-34. There was a large explosion, I was thrown by the blast, hit the back of my head very hard and lost consciousness. Time had stopped. I woke up from a strong pain at the bottom of my stomach, with blood seeping out of my nose and ears. I was shell-shocked but I still understood that I was wounded by shrapnel and that my comrades are trying get the the vehicle out of the battle. We didn’t go far when we had to stop at the roadside as the tank had run out of fuel. Even though we were very sorry for our loyal machine, there was no way we could leave it to the enemy. We had to steel ourselves against the pain in our hearts and blow our tank up. But we also needed to leave as the Germans were near. Having armed themselves with handguns and grenades our crew started to make its way through the forest towards our forces.
<French>: Notre bataillon a pris une position défensive près de Nevel avec pour ordre de stopper l'avancée ennemie vers Moscou. J'ai touché un char allemand au tout début de la bataille, mais son équipage a réussi à pointer son canon sur nous et peu après un obus perforant frappa la tourelle de notre T-34. Il y a eu une grosse explosion qui me projeta, je me suis cogné très fort l'arrière de la tête et perdis conscience. Le temps s'était arrêté. Je me suis réveillé à cause d'une forte douleur au fond de mon estomac, du sang coulant de mon nez et de mes oreilles. J'étais sous le choc mais j'ai vite compris que j'avais été blessé par des shrapnels et que mes camarades tentaient de sortir le char de la bataille. Nous ne sommes pas allés bien loin et avons dû arrêter le char en bord de route par manque de carburant. Même si nous étions désolés pour notre fidèle machine, nous ne pouvions absolument pas la laisser tomber entre les mains de l'ennemi. Nous avons dû prendre sur nous-mêmes et avons sabordé le char. Mais nous devions aussi nous enfuir, les allemands approchaient. Armé de pistolets et de grenades, notre équipage commença à se frayer un chemin à travers la forêt en direction de nos lignes.
<Italian>: Il nostro battaglione si è stabilito difensivamente vicino a Nevel con l'ordine di fermare l'avanzata del nemico verso Mosca. Ho colpito un carro tedesco all'inizio della battaglia ma l'equipaggio avversario ha rivolto il cannone verso di noi, subito dopo il loro proiettile ha colpito la torretta del nostro T-34. Ci fu una grossa esplosione, io venni scaraventato contro la parete, battei la nuca e svenni. Il tempo si fermò. Mi svegliai con un forte dolore alla base dello stomaco, con il sangue che fiottava dal naso e orecchie. Ero sotto shock ma in grado di capire che ero ferito da una scheggia e che i miei compagni stavano provando a portare in salvo il veicolo. Non andammo tanto lontano, fermammo il carro al lato della strada privo di carburante. Eravamo molto dispiaciuti di abbandonare la nostra leale macchina, ma non potevamo lasciarla al nemico. Decidemmo di farlo saltare in aria, con un nodo in gola ed il dolore nel cuore. Ma dovevamo anche scappare poichè i tedeschi erano vicini. Armati di pistole e granate, il nostro equipaggio iniziò a marciare attraverso la foresta per raggiungere gli alleati.
<German>: Our battalion assumed a defensive position near Nevel with an order to halt the enemy’s advance towards Moscow. I hit a German tank at the very beginning of the battle, but the tank’s crew managed to turn their gun at us, soon after their armor piercing shell hit the turret of our T-34. There was a large explosion, I was thrown by the blast, hit the back of my head very hard and lost consciousness. Time had stopped. I woke up from a strong pain at the bottom of my stomach, with blood seeping out of my nose and ears. I was shell-shocked but I still understood that I was wounded by shrapnel and that my comrades are trying get the the vehicle out of the battle. We didn’t go far when we had to stop at the roadside as the tank had run out of fuel. Even though we were very sorry for our loyal machine, there was no way we could leave it to the enemy. We had to steel ourselves against the pain in our hearts and blow our tank up. But we also needed to leave as the Germans were near. Having armed themselves with handguns and grenades our crew started to make its way through the forest towards our forces.
<Spanish>: Nuestro batallón asumió una posición defensiva cerca de Nevel con la orden de detener el avance del enemigo hacia Moscú. Al principio de la batalla alcancé a un tanque Alemán, pero la tripulación del tanque consiguió girar su cañón hacia nosotros, poco después su proyectil perforante alcanzó la torreta de nuestro T-34. Hubo una gran explosión, salí despedido por la explosión, me golpeé muy fuerte en la nuca y perdí el conocimiento. El tiempo se había detenido. Me desperté por un fuerte dolor en el fondo del estómago, con sangre saliendo de la nariz y los oídos. Estaba conmocionado por los proyectiles, pero aún así comprendí que estaba herido por la metralla y que mis compañeros estaban intentando sacar el vehículo de la batalla. No fuimos muy lejos cuando tuvimos que parar al borde de la carretera porque el tanque se había quedado sin combustible. Aunque lo sentimos mucho por nuestra fiel máquina, no podíamos dejarla en manos del enemigo. Tuvimos que endurecernos contra el dolor de nuestros corazones y hacer estallar nuestro tanque. Pero también teníamos que salir ya que los Alemanes estaban cerca. Tras armarse con pistolas y granadas, nuestra tripulación comenzó a abrirse camino a través del bosque hacia nuestras fuerzas.
<Russian>: Наш батальон занял оборону недалеко от Невеля с приказом остановить продвижение врага к Москве. В самом начале боя мне удалось подбить немецкий "панцер", но экипаж танка развернул пушку в нашу сторону, бронебойный снаряд ударил в башню нашему Т-34. Раздался сильный взрыв, меня швырнуло взрывной волной, я сильно ударился затылком и потерял сознание. Время остановилось. Очнулся от сильной боли внизу живота, из носа и ушей текла кровь. Контуженный, я всё-таки понял, что получил ранение осколками, но мои товарищи пытаются вывезти подбитую машину из боя. Немного проехав, мы остановились на обочине дороги – в танке кончилось горючее. Как ни жалко было наш верный танк, оставлять врагу его было нельзя. С щемящим сердцем нам пришлось взорвать нашу боевую машину. Но и нам нужно было уходить, немцы были совсем близко. Вооружившись пистолетами и гранатами, наш экипаж стал пробираться через лес в сторону наших войск.
<Polish>: Nasz batalion zajął pozycję obronną niedaleko Newelu z rozkazem zatrzymania natarcia wroga w kierunku Moskwy. Na samym początku bitwy trafiłem niemiecki czołg, ale załoga czołgu zdołała skierować swe działo w naszą stronę, niedługo potem ich pocisk przeciwpancerny trafił w wieżę naszego T-34. Nastąpiła duża eksplozja, zostałem rzucony przez wybuch, uderzając mocno tył głowy i tracąc przytomność. Czas zatrzymał się. Obudziłem się z silnym bólem w dolnej części brzucha, z krwią wyciekającą z nosa i uszu. Byłem wstrząśnięty, ale nadal rozumiałem, że zostałem ranny odłamkami i moi towarzysze próbują wydostać pojazd z bitwy. Nie pojechaliśmy daleko, kiedy musieliśmy zatrzymać się przy drodze, ponieważ czołgowi skończyło się paliwo. Choć bardzo nam było przykro z powodu naszej lojalnej maszyny, nie było sposobu, abyśmy mogli ją zostawić w rękach wroga. Musieliśmy przeciwstawić się bólowi w sercu i wysadzić nasz czołg. Ale musieliśmy też odejść, bo Niemcy byli blisko. Uzbrojena w pistolety i granaty, nasza załoga zaczęła przedzierać się przez las w kierunku naszych sił.

<Turkish>: Taburumuz, düşmanın Moskova'ya doğru ilerleyişini durdurmak için Nevel yakınlarında bir savunma pozisyonu aldı. Savaşın en başında bir Alman tankını vurdum, ancak tankın mürettebatı silahlarını bize çevirmeyi başardı, kısa süre sonra zırh delici mermileri T-34'ümüzün taretine isabet etti. Büyük bir patlama oldu, patlamanın etkisiyle savruldum, başımın arkasına çok sert bir darbe aldım ve bilincimi kaybettim. Zaman durmuştu. Karnımın alt kısmında şiddetli bir ağrıyla uyandım, burnumdan ve kulaklarımdan kan sızıyordu. Mermi şoku geçiriyordum ama yine de şarapnel parçasıyla yaralandığımı ve yoldaşlarımın aracı savaşın dışına çıkarmaya çalıştıklarını anladım. Tankın yakıtı bittiği için yol kenarında durmak zorunda kaldığımızda fazla uzaklaşmamıştık. Sadık makinemiz için çok üzgün olsak da onu düşmana bırakmamızın bir yolu yoktu. Kalbimizdeki acıya karşı kendimizi çelikleştirmeli ve tankımızı havaya uçurmalıydık. Ama aynı zamanda Almanlar yaklaştığı için oradan ayrılmamız gerekiyordu. Tabancalar ve el bombalarıyla silahlanan mürettebatımız ormanın içinden kuvvetlerimize doğru ilerlemeye başladı.

<Ukrainian>: Наш батальйон зайняв оборону недалеко від Невеля з наказом зупинити просування ворога до Москви. На самому початку бою мені вдалося підбити німецький "панцер", але екіпаж танка розвернув гармату в нашу сторону, бронебійний снаряд вдарив у башту нашому Т-34. Пролунав сильний вибух, мене кинуло вибуховою хвилею, я сильно вдарився потилицею і втратив свідомість. Час зупинився. Отямився від сильного болю внизу живота, з носа і вух текла кров. Контужений, я все-таки зрозумів, що отримав поранення осколками, але мої товариші намагаються вивезти підбиту машину з бою. Трохи проїхавши, ми зупинилися на узбіччі дороги - в танку скінчилося пальне. Як не шкода було наш вірний танк, залишати ворогові його було не можна. З щемливим серцем нам довелося підірвати нашу бойову машину. Але і нам потрібно було йти, німці були зовсім близько. Озброївшись пістолетами і гранатами, наш екіпаж став пробиратися через ліс в сторону наших військ.
<Serbian>: Naš bataljon je zauzeo defanzivnu poziciju blizu Nevela sa naredbom da zaustavi neprijateljsko napredovanje ka Moskvi. Pogodio sam Nemački tenk na samom početku bitke, ali je posada uspela da okrene cev ka nama a ubrzo zatim je njihova protiv oklopna granata pogodila kupolu naše T-34-ke. Osetila se strašna eksplozija, udar me je odbacio, udario sam glavom i pao u nesvest. Vreme je stalo. Došao sam svesti sa jakim bolom u dnu stomaka i krvlju koja je curila iz mog nosa i ušiju. Bio sam kontuzovan ali sam i shvatao da me je šrapnel pogodio i da moji drugovi pokušavaju da povuku vozilo iz bitke. Nismo stigli daleko kada smo morali stati pored puta kada nam je tenk ostao bez goriva. Iako nam je jako bilo žao naše verne mašine, nije bilo šanse da je ostavimo neprijatelju. Ignorišući bol u našim srcima razneli smo tenk. Morali smo krenuti jer su Nemci bili blizu. Naoružani sa pištoljima i granatama naša posada je krenula kroz šumu ka našim snagama.
<Hungarian>: A zászlóaljunk Nevel közelében vette fel a védekező állást, hogy megállítsuk az ellenség előrenyomulását Moszkva felé. A csata legelején eltaláltam egy német harckocsit, de a legénysége felénk tudta fordítani az ágyúját, nem sokkal később pedig egy páncéltörő lövedék eltalálta a T-34-ünk tornyát. Hatalmas robbanás volt, az ereje hátralökött, amitől bevertem a fejemet és elvesztettem az eszméletem. Az idő megállt. Erős fájdalommal tértem magamhoz a gyomrom alján, miközben az orromból és a füleimből vér szivárgott. Sokkot kaptam, de annyit még felfogtam, hogy repesztalálat ért, a társaim pedig megpróbálták kijuttatni a járművet a csatából. Nem jutottunk messzire, amikor meg kellett állnunk az út szélén, mert kifogyott az üzemanyag. Annak ellenére, hogy nagyon sajnáltuk a kis hűséges masinánkat, nem volt más választásunk, nem hagyhattuk ott az ellenségnek. Szörnyű érzés volt, amikor felrobbantottuk, de indulnunk kellett, mert a németek már közel jártak. Magunkhoz vettük a kézi fegyvereinket és a gránátokat, majd gyalog indultunk az erdőn át a csapataink felé.

<English>: Village after village, city after city, country after country — this is the way that the Soviet army of workers and peasants was freeing Europe from nazi invaders. We were met with thunderous cheers by the citizens of every city, we were given flowers by shy young girls and had old ladies bless us with the sign of the cross. We did not understand each other’s languages, but everything could be understood without a word – we gave freedom back to these people. Some were afraid of us and did not trust us, of course. They can be understood and it is not our place to judge them. And our way still lay ahead towards Germany. Our decisive battle was still ahead.

Nous ne parlions pas la même langue, mais nous nous comprenions sans dire un mot – nous avions rendu la liberté à ces personnes. Certains avaient peur de nous et ne nous faisaient pas confiance, évidemment. C'est compréhensible et ce n'est pas à nous de les juger. Notre chemin nous menait toujours vers l'Allemagne. La bataille décisive nous attendait.

<English>: Here it is. The accursed city of Berlin. It took us a long time to get here. That maniac Hitler has turned a beautiful city into a fortress – barricades covered with guns, its citizens scared to death, fascist propaganda keeps telling them that the Soviet soldier has come to have avenge what Germans did to their homes. I still remember these really young kids, armed with grenade launchers. Well, we had the right to ask for an eye for an eye and blood for blood. We saw charred land and torn bodies in our villages, women and children tortured to death. But we were not fighting German people – we fought the nazi plague that had Germany in its grip. We fought and beat them, but not the German nation, we beat the tyranny, slavery and oppression. Major Mikhail Pavlov, 1917-2011

Je me souviens encore de ces jeunes enfants, armés de lance-grenades. Eh bien, nous avions le droit de demander un oeil pour un oeil, le sang pour le sang. Nous avons vu des terres calcinées et des corps déchirés dans nos villages, des femmes et des enfants torturés à mort. <English>: After a word had reached us that the Allies landed in France, in Normandy to be precise, there was a harrowing silence among us. Having just fought off the onslaught in the mountains of northern Italy, it looked like a cruel joke, that the Allies were able to simply open up another front, elsewhere. But there was no time to contemplate. Assigned to a Tiger unit in western France, I was determined to drive the Allies back into the ocean.

Juste après avoir combattu dans les montagnes de l'Italie du nord, cela semblait être une blague cruelle, que les Alliés puissent simplement ouvrir un autre front, ailleurs. Mais nous n'avions pas le temps d'y réfléchir. Affecté à une unité de Tigre à l'ouest de la France, j'étais déterminé à repousser les Alliés dans l'océan.
<Italian>: Dopo che ci fosse pervenuta una voce che gli alleati sarebbero sbarcati in Francia, in Normandia per essere precisi, ci fu un silenzio straziante tra di noi. Ma non c'era tempo di pensare. Venni assegnato ad un'unità di Tiger in Francia occidentale, ero determinato a rigettare gli alleati indietro nell'oceano.

<English>: A week ago, we set out to a last ditch effort to push through the Ardennes, back into France. The war was lost, everyone knew that by now. With the Soviets closing in from the East, we wouldn’t stand a chance, even if we were successful here. Still, as soldiers, we were committed to fight and die for our fatherland. In Stuttgart we’ve been ambushed by American Shermans. Although we were successful with our Tiger at first, it was only a matter of time until we were knocked out. I can still see the faces of the young Americans who took us prisoners as we crawled out of our Tiger, even today. To them, it must have been like slaying a beast.

<English>: It’s now been more than seven decades since I last set foot into a Tiger, or any other military vehicle for that matter. Looking back, I am still scared by the amount of destruction that I and others have caused during this horrible war, blinded by youth and ambition. Living my last days on this earth as peaceful as possible, all I wish for is that no one ever has to endure the same.

Voglio vivere i miei ultimi giorni su questa terra il più piacevolmente possibile, ciò che desidero è che nessun'altro riviva tutto ciò.

<English>: This game mode is about the clash of two armies. Both armies have a specific setup of vehicles which are distributed randomly among the players. If all the vehicles are allocated out, it will not be possible to spawn. There are 3 vehicles available to choose from on each spawn for players (3 given at the start and 1 will be provided at each spawn). The vehicles can be either a single model or indeed different models.
<French>: Ce mode de jeu se base sur un conflit entre deux armées. Ces deux armées ont un setup spécifique de véhicules distribués aléatoirement entre les joueurs. Si tous les véhicules sont déjà attribués, il ne sera pas possible de réapparaître. Il y a 3 véhicules disponibles à chaque réapparition du joueur (3 donnés au début et 1 fourni à chaque réapparition). Les véhicules peuvent être du même modèle ou bien de modèles différents.
<Italian>: In questa modalità ci si scontra tra due eserciti. Entrambi gli eserciti hanno unità scelte specificatamente e sono distribuite casualmente tra i giocatori. Se tutte le unità sono scelte, non è possibile rigenerarsi. Ci sono 3 unità disponibili per essere scelte per i giocatori (3 date all'inizio ed 1 ad ogni rigenerazione). Le unità possono essere un modello singolo o molteplici modelli.

If all the vehicles are allocated out, it will not be possible to spawn. There are 3 vehicles available to choose from on each spawn for players (3 given at the start and 1 will be provided at each spawn). The vehicles can be either a single model or indeed different models.
<Spanish>: Este modo de juego consiste en el enfrentamiento de dos ejércitos. Ambos ejércitos tienen una configuración específica de vehículos que se distribuyen al azar entre los jugadores. Si todos los vehículos están repartidos, no será posible reaparecer. Hay 3 vehículos disponibles para elegir en cada reaparición para los jugadores (3 dados al principio y 1 será proporcionado en cada reaparición). Los vehículos pueden ser de un solo modelo o incluso de diferentes modelos.
<Russian>: В данном режиме обыгрывается столкновение двух армий. Обе армии имеют конечный набор техники который распределяется случайно между игроками. Если вся техника кончится спавниться будет больше нельзя. На каждом спавне игрокам доступно на выбор по 3 машины (3 даются на старте и по одной после каждого спавна). Машины могут быть как одной, так и разных моделей.
<Polish>: Ten tryb gry polega na starciu dwóch armii. Obie armie posiadają specyficzny zestaw maszyn, które są rozlosowane wśród graczy. Jeśli wszystkie maszyny zostały wykorzystane, odrodzenie nie będzie możliwe. Dostępne są 3 maszyny do odrodzenia dla graczy (3 dostępne na start i 1 dostępna przy każdym odrodzeniu). Maszyny mogą być jednakowe lub różne.
<Czech>: Střet dvou armád. Obě armády mají připravené sady strojů, které jsou rozděleny náhodně mezi hráče. Po nasazení všech strojů nebude možné nasadit žádný další. Pro hráče jsou na výběr tři stroje na každé nasazení (Tři na začátku a jeden na každé nasazení. Stroje můžou být stejného i různého typu.
<Turkish>: Bu oyun modu iki ordunun çatışması ile ilgilidir. Her iki ordu oyuncular arasında rastgele dağıtılan belirli bir sete sahip. Eğer bütün araçlar paylaştırılmış ise, doğmak mümkün olmayacaktır. Oyuncular için her doğuşta seçilebilecek 3 araç mevcut (Başlangıçta 3 tane verilir ve her doğuşta 1 tane sağlanır). Araçlar hem tek model veya gerçekten farklı modeller olabilir.

Hay 3 vehículos disponibles para elegir en cada reaparición para los jugadores (3 dados al principio y 1 será proporcionado en cada reaparición). Los vehículos pueden ser de un solo modelo o incluso de diferentes modelos.
<Russian>: В данном режиме обыгрывается столкновение двух армий. Обе армии имеют конечный набор техники который распределяется случайно между игроками. Если вся техника кончится спавниться будет больше нельзя. На каждом спавне игрокам доступно на выбор по 3 машины (3 даются на старте и по одной после каждого спавна). Машины могут быть как одной, так и разных моделей.
<Polish>: Ten tryb gry polega na starciu dwóch armii. Obie armie posiadają specyficzny zestaw maszyn, które są rozlosowane wśród graczy. Jeśli wszystkie maszyny zostały wykorzystane, odrodzenie nie będzie możliwe. Dostępne są 3 maszyny do odrodzenia dla graczy (3 dostępne na start i 1 dostępna przy każdym odrodzeniu). Maszyny mogą być jednakowe lub różne.
<Czech>: Střet dvou armád. Obě armády mají připravené sady strojů, které jsou rozděleny náhodně mezi hráče. Po nasazení všech strojů nebude možné nasadit žádný další. Pro hráče jsou na výběr tři stroje na každé nasazení (Tři na začátku a jeden na každé nasazení. Stroje můžou být stejného i různého typu.
<Turkish>: Bu oyun modu iki ordunun çatışması ile ilgilidir. Her iki ordu oyuncular arasında rastgele dağıtılan belirli bir sete sahip. Eğer bütün araçlar paylaştırılmış ise, doğmak mümkün olmayacaktır. Oyuncular için her doğuşta seçilebilecek 3 araç mevcut (Başlangıçta 3 tane verilir ve her doğuşta 1 tane sağlanır). Araçlar hem tek model veya gerçekten farklı modeller olabilir.

There are 3 vehicles available to choose from on each spawn for players (3 given at the start and 1 will be provided at each spawn). The vehicles can be either a single model or indeed different models.

Якщо вся техніка скінчиться відродження буде більше не можливе. На кожному відродженні гравцям доступно на вибір по 3 машини (3 даються на старті і по одній після кожного відродження). Vozila mogu biti pojedinačan ili različiti modeli.

<English>:
<color=@warningTextColor>Destroy ships using only torpedoes in order to gain <color=#2F2323>▊ </color>"Black Spots"!</color>
Our intelligence is reporting: large groups of ships under black flags close in to our support depots. Obviously, sea bandits decided to capture the warehouses and use them as transshipment bases. But don’t relax, a pirate is not a one-eyed one-legged bearded man but a skilled captain who will fight for his cargo till the bitter end!
<French>:
<color=@warningTextColor>Détruisez des bateaux en n'utilisant que des torpilles pour gagner des <color=#2F2323>▊ </color>"Marques Noires"!</color>
Nos informations: des flottes de bateaux sous pavillon noir s'approchent de nos dépôts. Les pirates ont apparemment décidés de capturer nos zones de stockage et de les utiliser comme base. Préparez vous, ces marins sont expérimentés et vont vous envoyer au fond de l'océan à la moindre occasion!
<Italian>:
<color=@warningTextColor>Distruggi le navi usando esclusivamente i siluri per ottenere <color=#2F2323>▊ </color>"Macchie Nere"!</color>
I servizi segreti hanno segnalato: una grande flotta navale con bandiera nera si sta avvicinando ai nostri depositi di supporto. Ovviamente i pirati decideranno di catturare i magazzini ed usarli come basi per il commercio. Non rilassarti, un pirata non è un uomo con una benda ed una gamba di legno ma un capitano astuto che combatterà per il suo carico fino alla fine!
<German>: <color=@warningTextColor>Zerstöre Schiffe ausschließlich mit Torpedos, um <color=#2F2323>▊ </color>Schwarze Flecken" zu verdienen!</color> Die Aufklärung berichtet, dass große Gruppen von Schiffen unter schwarzer Flagge auf unsere Versorgungsdepots zusteuern. Offenbar haben diese Seeräuber die Absicht, unsere Lagerstätten zu erobern und als Umschlagplatz zu missbrauchen. Habt keinen Zweifel: diese Piraten der Neuzeit sind keine einäugigen, einbeinigen Banditen mit Bart mehr - diese fähigen Kapitäne werden bis zum Schluss um die Ladung kämpfen!"
<Spanish>:
<color=@warningTextColor>¡Destruye buques usando solo torpedos para ganar <color=#2F2323>▊ </color>"Marcas Negras"!</color>
Nuestra inteligencia informa: grandes grupos de barcos con banderas negras se acercan a nuestros depósitos de apoyo. Evidentemente, los bandidos del mar han decidido capturar los depósitos y utilizarlos como bases de transbordo. Pero no te relajes, ¡un pirata no es un tuerto con barba, sino un hábil capitán que luchará por su cargamento hasta el amargo final!
<Russian>:
<color=@warningTextColor>Уничтожайте корабли только торпедами, чтобы заработать <color=#2F2323>▊ </color>"Чёрные метки"!</color>
Разведка докладывает: на наши складские базы движутся крупные группы военных кораблей под чёрными флагами. По всей вероятности, бандиты морей и океанов решили захватить склады и основать на их месте перевалочные базы, прибрав к рукам уже имеющееся содержимое. Но не расслабляйтесь. И пусть отныне, слыша "пират", вам представляется не одноногий, одноглазый бородач, а умелый капитан, готовый сражаться за свой ценный груз до последней монеты!
<Polish>:
<color=@warningTextColor>Zniszcz okręty za pomocą torped by zdobyć <color=#2F2323>▊ </color>"Czarne plamy"!</color>
Nasz wywiad donosi o dużej liczbie okrętów pod czarną banderą, które zbliżają się do naszych uzupełnień. Bandyci zdecydowali się na przejęcie zapasów i użycie ich jako bazy transportu morskiego. Uważajcie! Piraci to nie jednoocy ludzie z drewnianą nogą, lecz doświadczeni kapitanowie, którzy będą walczyć do końca!
<Czech>:
<color=@warningTextColor>Ničte lodě jen pomocí torpéd a získejte <color=#2F2323>▊ </color>"Černé tečky"!</color>
Ze zpráv rozvědky: u našich zásobovacích skladišť se nachází velké skupiny lodí pod pirátskou vlajkou. Korzáři se rozhodli zabrat skladiště a použít je jako překladiště pro pašování. Ale pozor: piráti nejsou jednoocí, jednonozí a vousatí muži, ale zkušení kapitáni, kteří budou o kořist bojovat až do hořkého konce!
<Turkish>:
<color=@warningTextColor>Sadece torpido kullanarak düşman gemilerini yok et ve şunu kazan <color=#2F2323>▊</color>''Siyah Noktalar''!</color>
Bizim istihbarat raporlarına göre: gruplar halinde ilerleyen siyah bayraklı gemiler destek depolarımızı kapattı. Görünüşe göre deniz korsanları depoları yakalama ve aktarma üsleri olarak kullanmaya karar verdi. Ama uyumak yok, bir korsan tek gözlü tek bacaklı ve sakallı bir adam olabilir ama sonuna kadar acı içinde kargo için mücadele edecek yetenekli bir kaptan değil!

<English>:
In the [Capture the Flag] mode, players will have to capture the enemy's Flag at the enemy point and bring it to allied point. The location of both points is marked on the minimap.

If you kill a player who carries an enemy Flag - the Flag falls to the ground. If the Flag is picked up by a teammate - he will continue to carry it. If the Flag is picked up by the player of the team whose Flag was stolen - the Flag returns to its original position. If the player of any teams delivered the Flag to his allied point - both Flags will return to their initial places.
<French>:
Dans le mode [Capturez le drapeau], les joueurs devront capturer le drapeau adverse au point ennemi et l'apporter sur le point allié. L'emplacement des deux points est indiqué sur la mini-carte.

Si vous tuez un joueur qui porte le drapeau ennemi, ce dernier tombe au sol. Si le drapeau est ramassé par un coéquipier - il continuera à le porter. Si le drapeau est ramassé par un joueur de l'équipe dont le drapeau a été volé - le drapeau revient à sa position original. Si un joueur de n'importe quel équipe a délivré le drapeau à sa point allié - les deux drapeaux retourneront à leurs places initiales.
<Italian>:
In modalità [Cattura La Bandiera], i giocatori dovranno catturare la bandiera nemica posta nel punto avversario e portarla fino al punto alleato. Il luogo di entrambi i punti è segnato sulla minimappa.

Se distruggi un giocatore che sta trasportando la bandiera - essa cade a terra. Se la bandiera viene raccolta da un compagno - continuerà a portarla. Se la bandiera viene raccolta dalla squadra a cui è stata rubata - la bandiera tornerà al punto di partenza. Se il giocatore di qualsiasi squadra porta la bandiera al suo punto alleato - entrambe le bandiere torneranno alla posizione di partenza.
<German>:
In 'Erobere die Flagge' müssen die Spieler die Flagge des Gegners erobern und zu ihrer eigenen Flagge bringen. Die Position beider Flaggenpunkte ist auf der taktischen Karte markiert.

Wird der Träger der gegnerischen Flagge zerstört, fällt die Flagge zuboden und kann von einem verbündeten Spieler erneut aufgehoben oder von einem Gegner zurückgesetzt werden.
<Spanish>:
En el modo [Captura la Bandera], los jugadores tendrán que capturar la Bandera del enemigo en el punto enemigo y llevarla al punto aliado. La ubicación de ambos puntos está marcada en el minimapa.

Si matas a un jugador que lleva una Bandera enemiga - la Bandera cae al suelo. Si la Bandera es recogida por un compañero de equipo - continuará llevándola. Si la Bandera es recogida por el jugador del equipo cuya Bandera fue robada - la Bandera vuelve a su posición original. Si el jugador de cualquier equipo entregó la Bandera a su punto aliado - ambas Banderas volverán a sus lugares iniciales.
<Russian>:
В режиме [Захват Флага] игрокам предстоит захватить Флаг противника на вражеской точке и принести его на союзную точку. Расположение обеих точек отмечено на миникарте.

Если убить игрока, который несёт Флаг противника - Флаг падает на землю. Если Флаг подбирает товарищ по команде - он продолжит его нести. Если Флаг поднимает игрок команды, чей Флаг был похищен - Флаг возращается в начальное положение. Если игрок одной из команд доставил Флаг на свою союзную точку - все Флаги вернутся на свои исходные места.

W trybie [Zdobądź flagę] gracze muszą zdobyć flagę przeciwnika w punkcie wroga i dostarczyć ją do punktu sojuszniczego. Lokalizacja obu punktów jest zaznaczona na minimapie. 

Jeśli zniszczysz gracza, który niesie flagę przeciwnika - flaga spadnie na ziemię. Jeśli flaga zostanie podniesiona przez członka drużyny - nadal będzie można ją donieść. Jeśli flaga zostanie podniesiona przez gracza z drużyny, której flaga została skradziona - flaga wraca do pierwotnej pozycji. Jeśli gracz dowolnej drużyny dostarczy flagę do punktu sojuszniczego - obie flagi wracają na swoje pierwotne miejsca.

<English>:
Presents, prizes and discounts - it’s all great, but sometimes you just want to have some fun. That’s why we have prepared two holiday fun events for you:
"Chasing Christmas" – Try capturing enemy Christmas tree while keeping yours safe or at least be the first to bring the other team’s tree home!

"Festive delivery" – Two teams of Christmas elves are helping Santa to gather presents. The team that brings the most presents wins.
<French>:
Des cadeaux, des récompenses et des rabais - c'est super, mais parfois on veut juste s'amuser un peu. C'est pourquoi nous avons préparé deux évènements amusants pour vous:
"À la poursuite de Noël" – Essayez de capturer le sapin de Noël ennemi tout en gardant le vôtre en sécurité ou soyez au moins le premier à ramener le sapin ennemi à votre base!

"Livraison festive" – Deux équipes d'elfes de Noël aident le Père Noël à recueillir des cadeaux. L'équipe qui rapporte le plus de cadeaux gagne.
<Italian>:
Regali, premi e sconti - è tutto magnifico, ma a volte devi solo divertirti.
Abbiamo preparato per te due settimane di eventi divertenti:
"Inseguire il Natale" - Prova a catturare l'albero di natale nemico tenendo al sicuro il tuo o almeno sii il primo a portare l'albero a casa!

"Consegne di Natale" - Due squadre degli elfi natalizi stanno aiutando Babbo Natale a portare i regali. La squadra che recupera più regali vince.
<German>:
Geschenke, Preise, und Rabatte - das ist alles gut, aber manchmal möchte man einfach nur ein bisschen Spaß haben. Deshalb haben wir zwei muntere Feiertagsevents für euch:

"Festliche Lieferung" - Zwei Teams von Weihnachtselfen helfen dem Weihnachtsmann Geschenke zu sammeln. Das Team, das die meisten Geschenke bringt, gewinnt.

<English>:
In the [Capture the Flag] mode, players will have to capture the enemy's Flag at the enemy point and bring it to allied point. The location of both points is marked on the minimap.

If you kill a player who carries an enemy Flag - the Flag falls to the ground. If the Flag is picked up by a teammate - he will continue to carry it. If the Flag is picked up by the player of the team whose Flag was stolen - the Flag returns to its original position. If the player of any teams delivered the Flag to his allied point - both Flags will return to their initial places.

For 1 victory in this event you will receive the "Flag of Victory" decal. For every five battles you will receive a "Victory Trophy".

Dans le mode [Capturez le drapeau], les joueurs devront capturer le drapeau adverse au point ennemi et l'apporter sur le point allié. L'emplacement des deux points est indiqué sur la mini-carte.

Si vous tuez un joueur qui porte le drapeau ennemi, ce dernier tombe au sol. Si le drapeau est ramassé par un coéquipier - il continuera à le porter. Si le drapeau est ramassé par un joueur de l'équipe dont le drapeau a été volé - le drapeau revient à sa position original. Si un joueur de n'importe quel équipe a délivré le drapeau à sa point allié - les deux drapeaux retourneront à leurs places initiales.

Pour une victoire à cette évènement vous recevrez la décalcomanie "Drapeau de la Victoire". Toutes les 5 batailles, vous recevrez un "Trophée de la Victoire".

Se distruggi un giocatore che sta portando la Bandiera - essa cadrà al suolo. Se la Bandiera viene raccolta da un compagno - dovrà continuare a portarla. Se la Bandiera viene raccolta dal giocatore a cui la Bandiera è stata rubata - la Bandiera tornerà alla posizione originaria. Se il giocatore di qualsiasi squadra porta la Bandiera fino al punto alleato - entrambe le bandiere torneranno al punto di partenza.

<English>:
Become the last player alive among dozens of opponents in a shrinking battle area! Pick the loot up on the map to defeat all enemies - blow them up with powerful artillery or repair all modules and restore the crew in your tank in the battle. Choose tactics and find your optimal tank that will bring victory in the tournament with prizes!

You can track your progress and the number of destroyed enemies by clicking "Leaderboard". 

<color=@warningTextColor>The Gladiator helmet (Gold) coupon</color> for the 100 best in each game mode will be credited after an additional check of the winners within 3 days from the end of the tournament.
<French>:
Soyez le dernier joueur en vie parmi une douzaine d'opposants dans une zone de combat qui rétrécit! Ramassez du butin sur la carte pour défaire vos ennemis - détruisez les avec une puissante artillerie ou réparez vos modules et restaurez votre équipage en plein combat. Choisissez vos tactiques et trouvez le char optimal qui vous apportera la victoire dans ce tournoi avec des récompenses!

Vous pouvez suivre votre progrès et le nombre d'ennemis détruits en cliquant sur "Leaderboard".

<color=@warningTextColor>Le coupon pour le casque de Gladiateur (Or)</color> pour les 100 meilleurs joueurs dans chaque mode sera attribué après une dernière vérification des vainqueurs dans une période de 3 jours après la fin du tournoi.

Sii l'ultimo giocatore sopravvissuto tra dozzine di avversari in un'area di battaglia che si restringe! Prendi il bottino nella mappa per sconfiggere tutti i nemici - falli esplodere con una potente artiglieria o ripara tutti i moduli e recupera l'equipaggio in battaglia. Scegli la tattica e trova il tuo carro armato ottimale che può portarti alla vittoria nel torneo con premi!

Puoi controllare i tuoi progressi ed il numero di nemici distrutti nella "Classifica". 

<color=@warningTextColor>Coupon per l'elmetto da Gladiatore (Oro)</color> per i primi 100 migliori giocatori in ciascuna modalità verranno ricompensati dopo il controllo dei vincitori nei 3 giorni dopo la fine del torneo.
